principle: Share what a thing MEANS. Never share what it LOOKS like. A shared visible renderer would turn seven concepts into one application in seven skins, which is the failure this pass exists to remove.

presentation_roles_this_concept_owns: Home composition — search, one attention block, then a two-column grid of destination cards over a compact text rail of the twelve areas
Navigation geometry — compact left text rail plus a card grid; the card expands in place into the area it names
Manager composition — roster at a fixed 280px with the selected object's form filling the rest of one pane; subpages are a quiet tab strip above the form
Exact-result reveal — the destination row lifts and takes a soft ring that fades once, originating at the row
Narrow-width transformation — the rail pushes off-screen, the grid becomes one column, roster and form become two pushed pages
Motion metaphor — expand-and-transfer: the thing you pressed becomes the thing you get
Density and typography — medium-tight, 13px body, 1.45 line height, 12px row rhythm
shared_headless_modules_consumed: shared/pm-shell.css and shared/pm-shell.js (PM application chrome only)
concept_specific.no_second_owner: This concept creates no scheduler, no progress owner, no balance calculator, no binary resolver and no second Project identity.

components.detail: Every operation the concepts open asks the one governor for a permit and renders the answer. No concept schedules, queues or admits work.
The only progress and wait projection. Determinate progress appears solely with a real denominator; otherwise an honest indeterminate state with a named wait reason.
Detection, identity, binding, staging, verification and rollback of provider installations. Settings shows its answers and starts its operations; it never resolves a binary itself.
Readiness comes from the provider lifecycle, balances from Usage. Settings configures the boundary — what happens when included usage ends — and computes neither.
One Project is the subject of every editable value. The concepts show it as context and never as a selector.
Human-only. No concept renders, drives or automates a sign-in surface; authentication is handed to the provider's own login.

The projection of the canonical inventory into domain, page, section, exposure and record kind. Data and semantics only — it draws nothing. Implemented here as shared2/pm2-inventory.js plus pm2-model.js.
Immutable result ids, grouped bounded results, typo tolerance and destination objects. One index, seven completely different dropdowns.
A destination is an object — domain, page, section, row, manager, object, subpage — not a string. Every concept parses and writes the same grammar and renders it differently.

What a manager contains, what each row means, which word describes a status, what an action claims to do. Each concept writes exactly one renderer against it, which is what stops forty-four managers becoming three hundred hand-written screens.
Preview, restore point, atomic apply, verification, receipt and rollback, with the credential-reference policy stated once.
The nineteen deterministic situations, addressable from the route so a screen can be handed to someone else exactly.
The vocabulary is shared; the row is not. Each concept lays out title, explanation, control and status in its own rhythm.
Deliberately seven different answers. Sharing these would collapse the bakeoff into one application in seven skins, which is the failure this pass exists to avoid.
Composition, entry, exit and motion are the concept's. Only the spec beneath them is shared.
The contract is absolute — secret material is never read, rendered or exported — and every concept renders the reference in its own idiom.

verification: The manager-route matrix records, per manager, that the surface rendered is this concept's own and that no string in any spec names another concept page. The static suite fails the build if a concept file references opus-5-atlas/console/stack/ledger, another concept-NN page, or an iframe.
